verdict.rationale: Channel3 publishes a downloadable OpenAPI 3.1.0 description of its API, and the API is /v1 path-versioned with a dated semver changelog. That gives developers a readable, versioned spec of the interface it speaks. However, the spec's info block carries framework defaults ("FastAPI", "0.1.0") rather than a real spec version, and it describes a proprietary API rather than an open commerce protocol. The UCP support mentioned in the docs is not shown to be backed by any spec Channel3 publishes. missing for 10: a versioned open protocol specification (e.g. a UCP spec published or linked by Channel3), meaningful version metadata in the spec itself, an explicit statement that it can be read and implemented without any agreement, and independent corroboration that the spec is accessible.

support.subject: As a developer, the commerce protocol this product speaks is published as an open, versioned specification I can read and implement without signing anything

citations.quote: Channel3 publishes a downloadable OpenAPI 3.1.0 document (48 paths plus 5 webhooks, production server https://api.trychannel3.com)
If your agent already supports UCP, connect it to Channel3's global catalog for product search and lookup across stores.
